title: The Villa
description: A handsome 19th-century stone residence situated near the Rectory grounds. Built during Houghton-le-Spring's Victorian expansion, it reflects the prosperous residential character of the town during the height of its local coal-mining and brewing eras.

title: The Rectory & Rectory Park
description: The historic grounds of the former Rector's residence, home to the natural freshwater spring that gives Houghton-le-Spring its name. Famous for the hospitality of Bernard Gilpin, who fed villagers and travellers here every Sunday.

title: South Wall – Bee Boles
description: Small, square-headed stone recesses built into the historic southern boundary wall of the old Rectory garden. These bee boles sheltered woven straw beehives (skeps) from northern winds while catching the sun's warmth to produce honey and church candle wax.

title: The Stone Arch
description: A surviving historic stone archway marking the gateway into the former Rectory grounds. It stands as a physical boundary between the bustling church and market area and the peaceful ecclesiastical estate.

title: St Michael and All Angels Church
description: Dating back to Norman times, this cruciform parish church has stood at the centre of Houghton-le-Spring life for over 800 years. Inside lies the ornate 16th-century tomb of Bernard Gilpin, known as the 'Apostle of the North'.

title: Kepier Hall
description: Founded under a Royal Charter from Queen Elizabeth I by Bernard Gilpin and John Heath as the Royal Kepier Grammar School. For centuries it educated generations of scholars before becoming a vibrant community hub managed by Acumen Community Buildings CIC.

title: The Almshouses
description: Endowed in the 1660s by George Lilburne and George Davenport immediately adjacent to Kepier Hall, these historic stone almshouses provided free shelter and support for six poor, elderly residents of the parish.

title: Houghton Brewery
description: Fed by Houghton's pure local spring water, brewing was a major industry in the town. Robinson Bros. Brewers Ltd operated here on a large scale, producing famous Houghton Ales that supplied pubs across County Durham and Sunderland.

title: Houghton Hall
description: Built in the early 17th century by Robert Hutton, nephew of the Archbishop of York. With its symmetrical stone facade, mullioned windows, and Dutch-style gables, it is one of the finest surviving Jacobean manor houses in North East England.

title: Nesham Place
description: Named after the prominent local Nesham family, this historic street features 18th- and 19th-century stone townhouses and cottages that formed the residential and social heart of old Houghton-le-Spring.
